headline: People doing things
intro: When asked what sort of paintings he did, Richard replied 'Subjective narrative paintings' when they looked perplexed he said 'People doing things'  These paintings and drawings are built from sketches, memory and the process of painting itself. Made in a studio in West Cornwall.

welcome_photo.caption: Richard in his studio, West Cornwall

welcome_text:
Richard Sorrell was born in 1948 into a family of artists: his father was the draughtsman and painter Alan Sorrell, his mother the watercolourist Elizabeth Sorrell.

After training at Kingston and the Royal Academy Schools, he spent some twenty-five years painting landscape, still life and aerial views of great houses for the National Trust. Today he paints invented pictures of people and places, from sketches, memory and imagination, in his studio near Penzance.

He is a past President of the Royal Watercolour Society, a member of the Royal Society of British Artists and the New English Art Club, and shows at the Royal Academy Summer Exhibition.

about_lede: The pictures are inventions, or reinventions of reality. Sometimes they may appear a little awkward and strange, but it is their awkwardness that gives them the power to communicate.
about_text:
Richard Sorrell was born in 1948, the son of the historical draughtsman and painter Alan Sorrell and the watercolourist Elizabeth Sorrell. He studied at Walthamstow Art School, Kingston College of Art and the Royal Academy Schools.

For around 25 years, living in London and Norfolk, he painted landscape, still life and portraits, and became known for aerial views of great houses for the National Trust and private owners. Over the past two decades the invented paintings have come to the fore, alongside an interest in sculpture, gardens and planting.

He was elected to the Royal Watercolour Society in 1975 and served as its President from 2006 to 2009.
